title: Review of active lifted theta directions

parts: Please review the brainstorming done with chatgpt in the folder /Users/teddy/Documents/shifted-zeta-positivity/papers/investigations-2/brainstorm, review the projects in investigations-2/active, and suggest any new directions. The main interesting area of research is currently finding new symmetries of the theta function from the lifted picture in quasi-rh-exponent-descent. Please see the recent chat in investigations-2/chat-histories. Please record this chat in that folder as well.
Note I just pulled a new commit with a new research branch and some analysis from chatgpt

I've written the review of the brainstorm and the 17 active projects, including the new GPT‑astra commit, with a set of new directions. I agree with GPT‑astra's ranking (02 and 01 first, 03 and 06 as destinations), with changes. A checking pass found four errors in my draft, all now fixed.

**The main conclusion.** The theta function is already pinned down by two symmetries: the reflection u → −u (the functional equation) and the integer lattice law. GPT‑astra's elliptic rigidity is the angular form of this; Hamburger's theorem is the scalar form. So a new symmetry can't make the source "more unique". It only helps if it survives the Newman deformation as a relation with a sign.

**New directions:**
- **A. Rank‑two automorphic lift.** This is where your intuition holds in a precise sense.
  - The paired kernels (card 09, already written out as Note 8, eq. (10) in project 17) are the non‑holomorphic Eisenstein series on the imaginary‑axis geodesic.
  - The full modular group, including the T symmetry that the Newman weight destroys in rank one, acts on the shape of the lattice ℤ², transverse to the physical direction.
  - The Newman weight then splits into a smoothing of the spectral parameter, which commutes with the modular group, and an explicit weight along the geodesic.
  - I derived an exact formula for the first Laguerre expression of ξ in these terms and checked it numerically to about 10⁻¹¹ at six heights, including the first zero. At the heights of the zeros, the Hecke (cusp) part carries essentially all of it.
- **Euler‑factor controls.** Perturb ζ's Euler factor at a single prime. The result is a positive even source with exactly ξ's real zeros and every other Euler factor intact, yet with de Bruijn–Newman constant Λ > 0. Consequence: any proof that Λ ≤ 0 must use the Euler factor at every prime. Every proposed identity should be tested on these.
- **02 (angular gluing).** The lattice law commutes with the Newman weight, so all defects come from the physical insertion. The Lagarias–Li Hecke operators turn out to be dilations and don't distinguish theta from the controls. GPT‑astra's planned period transport will likely just recover "all Dirichlet coefficients equal one", so I've given it a stop rule.
- **01 (cutoff reflection).** Start from Riemann's exact integral (Mordell‑type remainder) and Polymath's exact formula (39), rather than the stationary‑phase inversion.

**Other projects:** I recommend closing or merging 04, 07, 10, 11, 14, 15 and 16 (their targets are charts of the same quadratic forms, or generic to any positive source). Project 17 is correct but amounts to zero counting in topological form, so it deserves one cost benchmark and nothing more yet.

The four errors the checking pass caught were a reversed inequality, Polymath's A+B−C being an approximation rather than exact, a deformation endpoint I suggested that doesn't satisfy RH, and Lagarias's operator being skew‑adjoint rather than self‑adjoint.

The review is in `brainstorm/reviews`, with its checker and record in `brainstorm/numerics` (both re‑run on your machine). I added short pointers to the brainstorm, numerics and active READMEs and saved a summary to the project. I didn't create or move folders and didn't commit. The chat is recorded as chat 1 in `investigations-2/chat-histories/claude-cowork`, with its README entry added; the capture reported no gaps, and this reply enters with the next refresh. Should I set up direction A as an active folder?

**The Codex overlap.** Codex's angular-gluing calculation (02) is the one my review predicted: an exact identity with no sign. It also found two problems I hadn't anticipated, a divergent full-line version and a negative source value at the origin. Codex's own recommended next step was the "09-to-06" calculation, which is what the new folder 18 now does. So I've changed my recommendation for 02 from "first group" to "pause at its gate".

**Close/merge note** (`active/CLOSE_AND_MERGE_RECOMMENDATIONS_CLAUDE_20261013.md`). It is recommendations only; no folders were moved.
- **Pause:** 01 and 02, each at its own gate.
- **Merge:** 04, 10 and 11 into 06; 07, 09 and 15 into 18.
- **Close:** 14 and 16, plus 17, since its benchmark is done and showed no cost advantage.
- The working set becomes 18 and 19, with 08 optional.

**18, rank-two automorphic lift:**
- The physical insertion exactly cancels the Eisenstein constant term. That gives a formula for both Laguerre expressions, at every Newman time, in terms of the remaining (cusp) part alone. It matches direct computation to about 6·10⁻¹⁵.
- Card 09's two-coset identity is the Hecke relation at 2, which is the Euler factor at 2 in disguise.
- The control test is negative but useful. A control that differs from theta only at a prime p still satisfies the Hecke relation at every other prime, and still has Λ > 0. So no argument built on finitely many Hecke relations can prove Λ ≤ 0.
- No sign has appeared. One bounded task remains before the stop rule applies.

**19, Euler-factor controls:**
- A three-controls protocol that every new identity should be run against.
- An exact Newman-time formula for the controls.
- A one-point test: any real point where H_x² − HH_xx < 0 proves Λ > t, which makes rigorous lower bounds cheap to certify.
- A numerical table of Λ for the controls, which closely follows a simple formula of size 4·log(1/c)/(log p)².
- Λ > 0.2 for every prime p ≤ 41 at c = ½, which bears on the refereed bound Λ ≤ 0.2.
- Next step: certify Λ > 0.2 for p = 41 with outward-rounded arithmetic.

**Verification.** A separate Claude subagent rechecked the math with its own code at 20–30 digits. It found one error: my claim that the first mode dominates up to height 60 is false beyond about 42. It also flagged several overclaims. All are corrected, and its report is saved in `18_rank_two_automorphic_lift/reviews/`. Both checkers pass on your machine, and the repository hygiene check passes. Codex also caught an error of mine. Near a collision the raw witness margin shrinks, because L₀(H;X) = −2y²g² + y⁴L₀(g). Only the normalized ratio grows.

The one result in the lost note worth keeping is the N8 cross-check. √2 times Codex's raw same-parity response at the origin equals 18's twisted channel to within 9·10⁻¹⁵, and the value lies inside Codex's certified interval. I can restore it as a short reconciliation note that covers the raw split only.

Every lift so far has given exact identities but no sign. I now think there is a structural reason for that, and it shapes the ranking below.

## A. Bank what is nearly rigorous (do first)

**1. A short paper from 19.**
- Certify one fixed witness at t = 0.2 for (c, p) = (½, 41), with an absolute error budget.
- Write up the exact flow and the c = 1 transition. For c < 1 the Euler factor at p is non-tempered. For c > 1 it is tempered, and that control is RH-equivalent.
- Include the certified bound and the screening corollary in Codex's scoped form.
- A one-line mechanism explains t_m. To first order the flow multiplies the perturbation at p by e^{t(log p)²/4}, which is exactly Polymath's weight b_p^t. So T₀ ≈ t_m is the time at which the amplified local factor reaches the Ramanujan boundary.
- Stretch goal: prove Λ_{c,p} ≥ t_m − S₂t_m² − O(t_m³) unconditionally, using witnesses at x = π/a and Taylor bounds, and the matching upper bound under RH. That would give a de Bruijn–Newman constant of a natural family whose second-order term is ξ″(½)/2ξ(½).

**2. 18, after a single A4 run with a pre-registered prediction.**
- My prediction: the cusp modes reproduce the divisor-sum approximate functional equation for ζ(s)ζ(s′), which is the known main-sum and remainder structure.
- Check this on one cell against Polymath's A + B − C.
- If it matches, stop. Theorems 1–3 then become the section of the 19 paper explaining why finitely many Hecke relations are shared by the controls.

## B. One structural note to replace open-ended lift searches

Three facts seem to explain why the lifts give identities without signs.

- **Symmetry.** In rank d, theta is invariant under GL_d(ℤ) acting on lattices. The Newman weight is a Gaussian in the distance from the square lattice, so it is invariant under O(d). Their common group is the signed permutations B_d together with Poisson duality. On the rank-two flat this is sharp. If Φ(u₁)Φ(u₂) is invariant under a rotation by any angle that is not a multiple of π/2, then Φ is Gaussian (the Herschel–Maxwell argument). Every control has these symmetries.
- **Hecke under the flow.** T_p acts on the spectral parameter by multiplication by 2cos(ν log p), while the Newman flow is a heat flow in that same parameter. Moving one past the other turns real translations into the complex shifts x ± 2ita of 19's exact flow. So Hecke relations at t > 0 are deformed identities, shared by the controls at other primes.
- **Hamburger.** Integer frequencies, the Riemann gamma factor and conductor 1, with mild growth, characterize ζ. Each control breaks one of these. C1 has no integer frequencies, C2 is a sum of archimedean twists, and C3 has conductor p².

The deliverable would be a scoped checklist, not an impossibility theorem. A lifted relation can only carry information in three ways:
- using all the Hecke correspondences jointly and nonlinearly;
- importing positivity from another structure;
- evaluating the genuine function.

That is my honest answer to the "new symmetries" question: in the group sense, the lift has none that survive the flow.

## C. Lifted pictures where symmetry comes with positivity (pick one)

**3. The horocycle and bootstrap form of your exponent.**
- Zagier showed that RH holds if and only if long closed horocycles on SL₂(ℤ)\ℍ equidistribute with error o(y^{3/4−ε}).
- The same contour shift turns a zero-free half-plane Re s > β* into the rate y^{1−β*/2−ε}. So 7/8 gives 9/16, the conditional 33/41 gives 0.598, and RH gives 3/4.
- Benjamin and Chang restate RH as a statement about the asymptotic density of scalar operators in U(1)^c CFTs. They do this through a crossing equation that contains every zeta zero.
- This puts lattice-theta lifts (Narain lattices), built-in positivity (unitarity, positive measures) and the descent exponent in one place. It uses full SL₂(ℤ) invariance and integer spin, which level-p² analogues of C3 lack.
- First task: write out the dictionary and identify a positivity constraint that could improve the exponent for the Eisenstein data but not for the level-p² non-tempered analogues.
- Kill criterion: every constraint found holds equally for those analogues.

**4. The metaplectic engine of the 7/8 proof (cross-lane).**
- The one place in your program where a lifted theta symmetry has produced an inequality is Kubota's cubic theta on ℍ³.
- Liu's B_new ≈ 0.8749571 sits at the lane's stall (0.8749572), and he expects it to be optimal for that system of estimates. So re-optimizing won't move it, but a different theta might.
- Theta functions on n-fold covers of GL_r have unique Whittaker models, and so determined coefficients, only when n = r, or when n = r + 1 under a cocycle condition. The cubic theta on GL₂ is the case (r, n) = (2, 3). The cubic theta on GL₃ (Bump–Hoffstein) is the next case.
- First task: a one-page ledger of which theta property sets each exponent in the 7/8 proof. The candidates are the Gauss-sum coefficients on cn³, the constant term v^{2/3}, the Bessel function K_{1/3}, and the cubic and sextic sieves. Then work out what the GL₃ theta would change.
- Kill criterion: no candidate theta has a reflection formula of the needed shape.

## D. Smaller items

- **02.** Run the brief's multiplier search once, time-boxed. Add a kill test: the argument must visibly fail for a C3 control whose collision lies inside the declared rectangle, since those controls lack full gluing.
- **Cross-lane target.** The strip transfer Λ ≤ (2β*−1)²/2 beats 0.2 once β* < 0.8162. It beats Gomila's machine-checked but unrefereed 0.1787854 once β* < 0.7990. The conditional 33/41 step would give Λ ≤ 0.1859.
- **D4 (pushing Λ numerically).** Less attractive now that Gomila's claim exists, unless you want an independent check that could be refereed.

**Suggested order:** A1, then A2, then B, then one of C3 or C4.

Sources: [Benjamin–Chang, JHEP 11 (2022) 143](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/JHEP11(2022)143); [Verjovsky, statement of Zagier's criterion](https://ar5iv.arxiv.org/html/1711.03593); [Cai, Whittaker uniqueness for theta on GL_r covers](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1602.06614); [Bump–Hoffstein, Cubic metaplectic forms on GL(3)](https://sugaku.net/oa/W2044118611); [Polymath 15](https://www.arxiv.org/pdf/1904.12438); [Gomila's post](https://www.judegomila.com/posts/riemann-lambda-0.1787854) (via a [digest](https://zeli.app/story/49437165)); Liu, arXiv:2610.12234 (project file); `brainstorm/reviews/PORTFOLIO_CLOSURE_REVIEW_CODEX_20261013.md`.
